q: 1. The water from kitchens, bathrooms, wash basins is called
explain: Sullage is waste water from households that does not contain human excreta (from baths, kitchens, etc.).

q: 2. A sewer which receives storm water, surface run-off and sewage is called a
explain: A combined sewer carries both sanitary sewage (domestic/industrial) and storm water in a single pipe.

q: 3. A sewer which receives sewage from the collection system and conducts it to a point of final disposal is called a
explain: The outfall sewer is the final section of the sewer line that carries the collected sewage to the treatment plant or disposal point.

q: 4. A sewer which gets discharge from two or more main sewers is called
explain: A trunk sewer is a large pipe that receives sewage from multiple main sewers for transport to a treatment plant.

q: 5. The sanitation system in which a small portion of storm water enters sanitary sewers is known as
explain: In a partially separate system, sewage and storm water from roofs/pavements go into one pipe, while general street storm water goes into another.

q: 6. The storm sewers are essentially required to
options: avoid creation of unfavourable healthy conditions
improve the general appearance of the city
dispose off the first washings of early showers
explain: Storm sewers prevent flooding, remove dirty 'first wash' water from roads, and help maintain city hygiene during monsoon.

q: 7. According to Fanning's formula, the quantity of storm water (Q) in litres per seconds is given by
explain: Fanning's empirical formula for discharge estimation is $Q = CA^{5/6}$ where A is the area.

q: 8. The cross-section recommended for separate system of sewerage is
explain: Circular sewers are the most efficient and economical choice for separate systems where flow remains relatively constant.

q: 9. For large sewers, the maximum distance between manholes should be
explain: In larger, walkable sewers, manholes can be placed further apart, with 300m being a common maximum limit for cleaning operations.

q: 10. The minimum diameter of a manholes cover should be
explain: A 50cm diameter is the standard minimum to allow a worker to pass through comfortably.

q: 11. The equipment used for checking the levels of the sewer inverts is
explain: Boning rods (along with sight rails) are traditional tools used during excavation to ensure the sewer pipe is laid at the correct gradient.

q: 12. In one pipe system of plumbing, waste water is carried away from
explain: Waste water (sullage) from all these fixtures is collected into the same main pipe as human waste in this system.

q: 13. All anti-siphonage pipe is not required in
explain: A single stack system relies on a larger diameter pipe and carefully designed branches to prevent siphoning without needing a separate vent/anti-siphonage pipe.

q: 14. The underground structure in the form of a circular or rectangular tank for the purposes of admitting sewage into it from the intercepting chamber is called a
explain: A cesspool is a watertight underground tank used for the temporary collection and storage of sewage; it must be emptied periodically.

q: 15. In preliminary treatment of sewage, the operation which takes place, is
options: removal of fine dissolved organic material
removal of harmful bacteria and other organisms
explain: Preliminary treatment involves physical processes like screening and skimming to remove large floating objects and lighter materials like grease or oil.

q: 16. Grit chambers of a sewage plant are usually changed after
explain: Depending on the accumulation rate, grit is typically cleaned or removed from the chambers every 2 weeks to maintain efficiency.

q: 17. Grit should be removed from sewage before
options: their lifting by means of pump etc.
settling of sewage in sedimentation tank
explain: Grit removal is essential to protect pumps from abrasion, prevent pipe clogging, and ensure that primary sedimentation tanks are not filled with inorganic matter.

q: 18. When the sewage is to be distributed over a level area surrounded by dykes, the method is called
explain: Flooding involves applying sewage to a leveled area enclosed by small embankments (dykes) to allow it to seep into the soil.

q: 19. The bio-chemical treatment of sewage effluent is a process of
explain: Biological treatment uses bacteria to oxidize organic matter into stable inorganic compounds.

q: 20. For ordinary domestic sewage B.O.D. reaction is expected to get completed in about
explain: At 20°C, it takes approximately 20 days to complete the first stage (carbonaceous) of the BOD reaction.

q: 21. Usual population equivalent of B.O.D. is
explain: Population equivalent is used to compare industrial waste to domestic sewage; 80g of BOD per person per day is a common design value.

q: 22. B.O.D. test is standardized at
explain: The standard lab test for BOD is conducted at 20°C for a duration of 5 days ($BOD_5$).

q: 23. In a C.O.D. test the most common interference is caused by the ions of ...........
explain: Chloride ions react with silver sulfate (the catalyst) and can be oxidized by dichromate, which leads to falsely high COD results. Mercuric sulfate is usually added to complex the chlorides and eliminate this interference.

q: 24. Time taken for C.O.D. test is about ...........
explain: While a standard BOD test takes 5 days, a COD test is much faster, typically requiring about 2 to 3 hours of refluxing (boiling) to complete the chemical oxidation.

q: 25. An advantage of C.O.D. test over B.O.D. test is ...........
options: it oxidized all matter including toxins
it cannot oxidize benzene, pyridine etc.
it is relatively a quick process
biodegradable matter cannot be distinguished from the rest
explain: The primary practical advantage of COD is the speed (3 hours vs 5 days), allowing for rapid monitoring and control of treatment plant processes.

q: 26. Separate system is adopted in ............
options: areas where rain fall is distributed throughout the year
explain: In areas with frequent rain, a separate system prevents the treatment plant from being overwhelmed by rainwater while still managing sewage.

q: 27. In general 'Imperviousness' of any catchment shall be between ............
explain: The runoff coefficient varies based on surface type; a fully paved city might approach 95%, while a park might be as low as 1%.

q: 28. Sewer that collects sewage from toilets is called ............
explain: A lateral sewer is the first stage of the network, collecting sewage directly from individual house connections (toilets/sinks) and carrying it to a branch sewer.

q: 29. The length of the main sewer leading to treatment of disposal units is called ............
explain: The outfall sewer is the final length of the sewerage system that conveys the entire accumulated volume of sewage to the treatment plant or the point of final disposal.

q: 30. A manhole is provided ............
explain: Manholes are essential points of access for inspection and cleaning; they must be placed wherever there is a change in the sewer's alignment, gradient, or pipe diameter.

q: 31. When raw sewage is to be disposed off by dilution sewage should ............
options: be having a B.O.D. less than 150 mg/l
explain: Floating matter (grease, plastics, corks) creates an immediate aesthetic nuisance in rivers or lakes, so these must be removed via screening before dilution.

q: 32. The factor governing the detention period in a grit chamber is ............
explain: The detention time is calculated based on how long it takes for a particle to travel the length of the chamber at a specific horizontal flow velocity.

q: 33. B.O.D. removal of primary clarifier is ............
explain: Primary sedimentation removes 50-70% of suspended solids, which usually corresponds to a 30-40% reduction in the total Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD).

q: 34. A fundamental difference between sedimentation tank for water and sewage is ............
options: sewage sedimentation tanks have more depth
sludge from sewage sedimentation is to be removed more frequently
it can be final treatment of operation in water treatment
explain: In water treatment, sedimentation might be the final step before disinfection; in sewage treatment, it is almost always just a preliminary step before biological oxidation.

q: 35. Organic loading of RBC is expressed as ............
explain: Because it is a surface-based process, loading is measured by the amount of organic matter applied per unit area of the discs per day.
